sentences.text: Solicitor Rachel Dunne initiated the call and confirmed client Matthew Kerr can hear her.
Matthew Kerr is the client in this meeting.
The purpose of the meeting is to discuss a potential claim related to alleged abuse by a swimming coach when Kerr was a child.
The alleged abuse involved Brian Hollis, who was the coach of the junior squad at Harbridge Swimming Club.
Matthew Kerr joined the swimming club at age nine.
Brian Hollis became Kerr's coach when he moved up to the squad at age eleven.
The abuse occurred in the changing room after training, when other children had left.
Brian Hollis touched Matthew Kerr.
Matthew Kerr said he was made to touch Brian Hollis.
Brian Hollis told Matthew Kerr that touching him was part of being in the squad and that everyone did it.
The abuse occurred every Saturday morning after squad training.
The abuse occurred over a period of about two years, from when Kerr was eleven until he was nearly thirteen.
The abuse occurred roughly from 1996 to 1998.
The abuse stopped when Matthew Kerr quit swimming.
Matthew Kerr told his mother when he was 13.
Matthew Kerr's mother took him out of the club after he told her.
Matthew Kerr does not know if his mother reported the abuse to anyone.
Matthew Kerr told his wife Claire in 2020 about the abuse.
Matthew Kerr told his general practitioner (GP) about the abuse.
Matthew Kerr reported the abuse to the police in March of the previous year (implied to be 2023).
Matthew Kerr gave a statement to the police in March.
The police have interviewed Brian Hollis.
The police investigation is still ongoing.
Matthew Kerr has the details of the police officer, DC Farrow.
Matthew Kerr has heard from a boy in the squad who said Brian Hollis abused other boys.
Matthew Kerr has not seen any evidence of abuse in other boys.
Matthew Kerr has had anxiety for years, including panic attacks.
Matthew Kerr had counselling through work in 2021.
Matthew Kerr had three months off sick in 2021.
Matthew Kerr has sick notes from 2021.
